avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive antiplatelet effects increase bleeding risk; NSAIDs inhibit platelet aggregation
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or limit Vitamin E to <400 IU/day; monitor for bleeding signs

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Platelet inhibition combined with NSAID antiplatelet activity significantly elevates bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue ginkgo or use alternative to diclofenac; counsel on bleeding precautions

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates antiplatelet effects of diclofenac, increasing hemorrhage risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose garlic supplements; use culinary amounts only if necessary

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice root
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Sodium retention and fluid accumulation; NSAIDs impair renal function and enhance licorice-induced hypertension
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid licorice root; monitor blood pressure and renal function closely

caution_supplements.name: Ginger
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet properties; additive effect with diclofenac's platelet inhibition
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased bruising or bleeding; use moderate culinary doses

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: Antiplatelet and potential CYP2C9 inhibition; may slightly increase diclofenac levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for efficacy changes; observe for bleeding signs with high-dose supplements

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effects; synergistic with NSAID anticoagulation
caution_supplements.action: Use moderate doses; counsel on bleeding precautions

caution_supplements.name: Feverfew
caution_supplements.mechanism: Platelet aggregation inhibition; additive antiplatelet effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased bleeding tendency; consider alternative anti-inflammatory

avoid_foods.name: Excessive alcohol (>3 drinks/day)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Alcohol irritates GI mucosa; NSAIDs inhibit protective prostaglandins; combined effect dramatically increases gastric ulceration and GI bleeding risk
avoid_foods.action: Advise complete alcohol avoidance or strict limitation to ≤1 drink/day; counsel on GI bleeding symptoms

avoid_foods.name: Aspirin-containing foods/products
avoid_foods.mechanism: Combined NSAID + aspirin use increases GI bleeding risk and renal toxicity without improved anti-inflammatory benefit
avoid_foods.action: Avoid aspirin and aspirin-containing products; use diclofenac as sole NSAID

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: NSAIDs impair renal sodium handling and increase water retention; excess dietary sodium worsens fluid accumulation and hypertension
caution_foods.action: Recommend modest sodium restriction (<2300 mg/day); monitor blood pressure and weight

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay diclofenac absorption and increase peak GI irritation when taken with high-fat food
caution_foods.action: Take diclofenac with light meals or milk; avoid taking on empty stomach despite delayed absorption

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function, blood pressure, and signs of GI bleeding (dark stools, abdominal pain) regularly during diclofenac therapy. Assess cardiovascular risk and use lowest effective dose for shortest duration, especially in elderly or renally impaired patients.
